items.prompt: A square garden has a fence. There are 4 posts on each side. The corner posts count for both sides. How many posts are there in all?

figure.alt: A square fence with 4 posts along each side, counting the posts at both corners. Each corner post belongs to two sides.

options.why: Count again: 4 corners plus 2 middle posts on each side.
Each side has only 2 posts between its corners.
The corner posts are shared, so count them only once.
16 counts each corner post twice.

hints: Draw the square and mark the posts.
Each side has 2 corner posts and some posts in between.
Each side has 4 posts, and 2 of them are corners. How many are in between?
items.explanation: Each side has 2 posts between its corners, so there are 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 middle posts. Add the 4 corners: 8 + 4 = 12 posts.

solution.say: 4 sides with 4 posts each would be 16, but each corner is counted twice.
There are 4 corner posts counted twice.
Or count 4 corners and 2 middle posts on each side.

items.prompt: A small book has pages numbered 1 to 15. How many digits are printed to number all the pages?

options.why: 15 is the number of pages. Some page numbers have 2 digits.
Count the 2-digit pages again: 10 to 15 is 6 pages.
Pages 10 to 15 are 6 pages with 2 digits each, which is 12 digits.
Pages 1 to 9 need only 1 digit each.

hints: Some page numbers have 1 digit and some have 2.
Pages 1 to 9 have 1 digit each. Pages 10 to 15 have 2 digits each.
Count how many pages go from 10 to 15.
items.explanation: Pages 1 to 9 use 9 digits. Pages 10 to 15 are 6 pages with 2 digits each, which is 12 digits. In all, 9 + 12 = 21 digits.

solution.say: Pages 10 to 15: 6 pages, two digits each.

items.prompt: Four friends meet. Each friend shakes hands once with each of the others. How many handshakes are there?

options.why: Each friend shakes 3 hands, but there are 4 friends.
Make a list of all the pairs of friends.
Count each handshake only once.
12 counts every handshake twice, once for each friend.

hints: Give the friends letters: A, B, C, D.
List the pairs. A shakes hands with B, C and D.
Then B shakes with C and D. Do not count A and B again.
items.explanation: The pairs are AB, AC, AD, BC, BD and CD. That is 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 handshakes.

solution.say: A shakes hands with B, C and D.
B still needs C and D.

items.prompt: Ben writes all the numbers from 1 to 50. How many of them have at least one digit 3?

options.why: 4 is only 3, 13, 23 and 43. The numbers from 30 to 39 count too.
Many numbers in the 30s have a 3 too.
10 is just the numbers from 30 to 39. Others like 13 and 23 count too.
Did you miss the number 3 itself?

hints: Look at the ones digit and the tens digit separately.
Numbers with a 3 in the ones place: 3, 13, 23, and so on.
Numbers from 30 to 39 all have a 3 in the tens place.
items.explanation: Numbers with a 3 in the tens place are 30 to 39, which is 10 numbers. Numbers with a 3 only in the ones place are 3, 13, 23 and 43. So there are 10 + 4 = 14 numbers.

solution.say: 3 in the tens place: 30, 31, and so on up to 39.
3 in the ones place, not already counted: 3, 13, 23, 43.
33 was already counted with the 30s, so do not count it again.

items.prompt: A grid has 2 rows of 3 squares. An ant starts at the bottom left corner. It walks along the lines to the top right corner. It only moves right or up. How many different paths can it take?

figure.alt: A grid of 2 rows and 3 columns of squares. The ant starts at the bottom left corner and ends at the top right corner, walking along the grid lines.

options.why: 6 paths is the answer for a 2 by 2 grid. This grid is 3 squares long.
Some paths were counted twice. Write the number of paths at each corner.
Too many. Write the number of ways to reach each corner.
20 paths fit a 3 by 3 grid. This grid has only 2 rows.

hints: Every path goes right 3 times and up 2 times.
Write the number of ways to reach each corner, starting near the start.
Corners on the bottom line and on the left line can be reached in only 1 way.
items.explanation: Write at each corner the number of ways to reach it. Each number is the sum of the number to its left and the number below it. The top right corner gets 10.

solution.say: Bottom line of corners: each can be reached in 1 way.
Middle line of corners: add the number on the left and the number below.
Top line of corners: do the same.

items.prompt: How many 2-digit numbers have digits that add up to 5?

options.why: Do not forget 50. Its digits are 5 and 0.
05 is not a 2-digit number.
Count again. List them: 14, 23, and so on.

hints: The tens digit cannot be 0.
Start with tens digit 1: 1 + 4 = 5, so 14.
Try tens digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 in turn.
items.explanation: The numbers are 14, 23, 32, 41 and 50. So there are 5 of them.

solution.say: A tens digit of 0 is not allowed, so 05 does not count.

items.prompt: Jo rolls a red dice and a blue dice. In how many ways can the total be 9?

options.why: Red 3 and blue 6 is different from red 6 and blue 3.
Go through the red dice from 3 to 6 and check each one.
Each dice shows only 1 to 6, so a 1 or a 2 cannot be part of a total of 9.

hints: Red 3 and blue 6 is one way. Red 6 and blue 3 is another.
Go through the red dice from 1 to 6. What must the blue dice show?
If red shows 1 or 2, blue would need 8 or 7. That cannot happen.
items.explanation: The ways are red 3 with blue 6, red 4 with blue 5, red 5 with blue 4, and red 6 with blue 3. That is 4 ways.

solution.say: Red 1 or 2: blue would need 8 or 7. Not possible.

items.prompt: Ayu writes all the numbers from 1 to 30. How many times does she write the digit 2?

options.why: That is only the tens place. Add the 2s in the ones place.
Count the 2s in the ones place: 2, 12 and 22.
22 has two 2s. Count both.

hints: Count the 2s in the ones place and in the tens place separately.
Ones place: 2, 12, 22. Tens place: 20 to 29.
22 has a 2 in both places, so it gives two 2s.
items.explanation: The ones place has a 2 in 2, 12 and 22, which is 3 times. The tens place has a 2 in 20 to 29, which is 10 times. In all, 3 + 10 = 13.

solution.say: Add them. 22 is in both lists because it has two 2s.

items.prompt: Six dots are on a circle. Ali joins every dot to every other dot with a straight line. How many lines does he draw?

figure.alt: Six dots spaced evenly around a circle, at the corners of a hexagon.

hints: Start with one dot. How many lines go from it?
Each dot joins to 5 others. But each line joins 2 dots.
The first dot gives 5 lines. The next dot gives only 4 new lines.
items.explanation: The first dot joins to 5 others, the next adds 4 new lines, then 3, 2 and 1. That is 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15 lines.

solution.say: Dot 1 joins to the other 5 dots.
Dot 2 is already joined to dot 1, so it adds 4 new lines.
Keep going: 3, then 2, then 1 new line.

items.prompt: Rudi pays exactly Rp7.000. He has plenty of Rp1.000 coins, Rp2.000 notes and Rp5.000 notes. How many different ways can he pay?

figure.alt: Rudi's money: Rp1.000 coins, Rp2.000 notes and a Rp5.000 note. He has as many of each as he needs.

hints: Sort the ways by how many Rp5.000 notes he uses.
With one Rp5.000 note, he still needs Rp2.000 more.
With no Rp5.000 note, try 0, 1, 2 or 3 Rp2.000 notes.
items.explanation: With a Rp5.000 note, the other Rp2.000 is one Rp2.000 note or two Rp1.000 coins: 2 ways. Without it, he can use 3, 2, 1 or 0 Rp2.000 notes and fill up with coins: 4 ways. That is 2 + 4 = 6 ways.

solution.say: With one Rp5.000 note, Rp2.000 is left.
Without a Rp5.000 note, use 3 or 2 Rp2.000 notes.

items.prompt: Ibu membuat 3 jenis kue: lapis, onde-onde, dan klepon. Ani boleh mengambil 2 kue yang berbeda jenis. Ada berapa pilihan untuk Ani?

options.why: Coba daftar semua pasangan kue.
Ada pasangan yang terhitung dua kali. Lapis dan klepon sama dengan klepon dan lapis.
Urutan tidak penting. Lapis lalu klepon sama dengan klepon lalu lapis.

hints: Buat daftar pasangan kue.
Mulai dari lapis. Lapis bisa dipasangkan dengan onde-onde atau klepon.
Sesudah itu, pasangan apa lagi yang belum ada?
items.explanation: Pasangannya lapis dan onde-onde, lapis dan klepon, serta onde-onde dan klepon. Jadi ada 3 pilihan.

items.prompt: Ada 5 anak dalam satu kelompok. Setiap anak mengirim satu kartu ucapan kepada setiap anak lain. Berapa kartu yang dikirim semuanya?

options.why: 10 adalah banyak jabat tangan. Kartu dikirim dua arah: A ke B dan B ke A.
Setiap anak mengirim 4 kartu. Hitung lagi untuk 5 anak.
Anak tidak mengirim kartu kepada dirinya sendiri.

hints: Hitung dulu kartu yang dikirim oleh satu anak.
Satu anak mengirim kartu kepada semua anak lain, yaitu 4 anak.
Ada 5 anak, dan setiap anak mengirim 4 kartu.
items.explanation: Setiap anak mengirim 4 kartu. Ada 5 anak, jadi kartunya 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 20.

solution.say: Satu anak mengirim ke 4 anak lain.
Berbeda dengan jabat tangan: kartu dari A ke B dan dari B ke A adalah 2 kartu.

items.prompt: A stall sells 2 drinks: tea and juice. It sells 3 snacks: bread, banana fritters and tofu. Leo buys 1 drink and 1 snack. How many different choices can he make?

head: Drinks
Snacks
figure.alt: A menu. Drinks: tea and juice. Snacks: bread, banana fritters and tofu.

options.why: 5 is 2 + 3. Each drink can go with every snack.
Try a list: tea with each snack, then juice with each snack.
There are only 2 drinks, not 3.

hints: Make a list of all the pairs.
Start with tea. Tea can go with bread, banana fritters or tofu.
Now do the same for juice.
items.explanation: Tea goes with 3 snacks and juice goes with 3 snacks. That is 3 + 3 = 6 choices.

solution.show: tea + bread, tea + fritters, tea + tofu
juice + bread, juice + fritters, juice + tofu

items.prompt: A locker code has 2 digits. Each digit can be 1, 2 or 3. Digits may repeat, like 33. How many different codes are there?

options.why: There are many more. List the codes that start with 1, then 2, then 3.
Codes like 11, 22 and 33 are allowed too.
Count again. Each first digit goes with 3 second digits.

hints: List the codes in order.
Codes that start with 1: 11, 12, 13.
Now list the codes that start with 2, then with 3.
items.explanation: Each of the 3 first digits can go with each of the 3 second digits. That is 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 codes.

items.prompt: A strip is made of 4 squares in a row. How many rectangles can you find in it? Squares count as rectangles too.

figure.alt: A strip of 4 squares in a row.

hints: Count rectangles by length: 1 square long, 2 long, 3 long and 4 long.
Rectangles 1 square long: there are 4 of them.
A rectangle 2 squares long can start at square 1, 2 or 3.
items.explanation: There are 4 rectangles 1 square long, 3 that are 2 long, 2 that are 3 long and 1 that is 4 long. That is 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

items.prompt: Four friends meet. Each friend shakes hands once with each of the others. How many handshakes are there?
hints: Call the friends A, B, C and D.
A shakes hands with 3 friends.
B has already shaken hands with A. Count B's new handshakes.
items.explanation: A shakes hands with 3 friends. B shakes with 2 new friends. C shakes with 1 new friend. That makes 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 handshakes.

items.prompt: Five children meet. Each child shakes hands once with each of the others. How many handshakes are there?
hints: Count the handshakes one child at a time.
The first child shakes 4 hands.
The next child has only 3 new handshakes.
items.explanation: The handshakes are 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10. Each pair of children shakes hands only once.

solution.say: Each pair of children shakes hands only once.

items.prompt: Six children meet. Every pair of children plays one game of noughts and crosses. How many games are played?
hints: Think about pairs of children.
The first child is in 5 pairs.
The next child has 4 new pairs.
items.explanation: The pairs are 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15. Each pair plays one game, so there are 15 games.

solution.say: Each pair plays one game, so there are 15 games.

items.prompt: 5 teams play a league. Each team plays every other team twice, at home and away. How many games are played?
hints: First count the games when each pair of teams plays only once.
5 teams make 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 games.
Every game is played twice.
items.explanation: When each pair plays once, there are 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 games. Each pair plays twice, so 10 x 2 = 20 games.

solution.say: When each pair plays once, there are 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 games.
Each pair plays twice, so 10 x 2 = 20 games.

items.prompt: A domino set uses the numbers 0, 1, 2 and 3. Each pair of numbers appears once. Each number also pairs with itself. How many dominoes are there?
hints: List the dominoes that start with 0: 0-0, 0-1 ...
There are 4 of those. Then list the ones that start with 1, but not 1-0.
3 start with 1, 2 start with 2, 1 starts with 3.
items.explanation: The dominoes that start with 0 are 4. Those that start with 1 and are new are 3. Then 2, then 1. In all, 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 dominoes.

solution.say: The dominoes that start with 0 are 4.
Those that start with 1 and are new are 3.

items.prompt: Mia has 3 shirts and 2 pairs of shorts. How many different outfits can she make?
hints: Pick one shirt. How many pairs of shorts can go with it?
Each shirt can go with 2 pairs of shorts.
There are 3 shirts.
items.explanation: Each of the 3 shirts goes with 2 pairs of shorts. That makes 3 x 2 = 6 outfits.

solution.say: Each of the 3 shirts goes with 2 pairs of shorts.

items.prompt: There are 3 flavours of ice cream and 2 kinds of cone. A cone holds 1 scoop. How many different ice creams can you make?
hints: Choose the kind of cone first.
With one kind of cone, there are 3 flavours to choose.
There are 2 kinds of cone.
items.explanation: For each of the 2 cones there are 3 flavours. So 2 x 3 = 6 different cones.

solution.say: For each of the 2 cones there are 3 flavours.

items.prompt: Ravi has 3 shirts, 2 pairs of shorts and 2 hats. How many different outfits can he make?
hints: First count the shirt and shorts together.
3 shirts and 2 pairs of shorts make 6 outfits.
Each of those can have either of the 2 hats.
items.explanation: Shirt and shorts make 3 x 2 = 6 outfits. Each can have 2 hats. So 6 x 2 = 12 outfits.

solution.say: Shirt and shorts make 3 x 2 = 6 outfits.

items.prompt: An ice cream has 2 different scoops. There are 4 flavours: vanilla, mango, coconut and chocolate. The order of the scoops does not matter. How many different ice creams are there?
hints: List the pairs that include vanilla.
Vanilla with mango, with coconut and with chocolate.
Then list the new pairs that include mango, but not vanilla.
items.explanation: The pairs are vanilla with 3 others, then mango with 2 new others, then coconut and chocolate. That is 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 ice creams.

solution.say: The pairs are vanilla with 3 others, then mango with 2 new others, then coconut and chocolate.

items.prompt: Use the digits 1, 2 and 3 to make 2-digit numbers. The two digits must be different. How many numbers can you make?
hints: List the numbers that start with 1.
They are 12 and 13.
Then list the ones that start with 2 and 3.
items.explanation: Starting with 1: 12, 13. Starting with 2: 21, 23. Starting with 3: 31, 32. That makes 6 numbers.

items.prompt: Make 3-digit numbers with the digits 0, 1 and 2 once each. A number cannot start with 0. How many can you make?
hints: The first digit can only be 1 or 2.
If the first digit is 1, the other two digits are 0 and 2.
List the numbers for each first digit.
items.explanation: Starting with 1: 102, 120. Starting with 2: 201, 210. A number cannot start with 0. That makes 4 numbers.

items.prompt: In how many different ways can 3 children stand in a line?
hints: Pick who stands first. There are 3 choices.
Then there are 2 children left for the second place.
The last child has only one place left.
items.explanation: There are 3 choices for first place, 2 for second place and 1 for last. So 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 ways.

solution.say: There are 3 choices for first place, 2 for second place and 1 for last.

items.prompt: In how many different ways can 4 children stand in a line?
hints: There are 4 choices for the first place.
Then there are 3 children left for the second place.
Multiply the choices: 4 x 3 ...
items.explanation: There are 4 choices for the first place, then 3, then 2, then 1. So 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 24 ways.

solution.say: There are 4 choices for the first place, then 3, then 2, then 1.

items.prompt: How many 2-digit numbers have two digits that are the same?
hints: The numbers start with 11.
Which is the last number?
items.explanation: The numbers are 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88 and 99. That makes 9 numbers.

items.prompt: Write the numbers from 1 to 50. How many times do you write the digit 9?
hints: Look at the ones place and the tens place.
Which numbers up to 50 have 9 in the ones place?
There is no number with 9 in the tens place before 50.
items.explanation: The digit 9 is in 9, 19, 29, 39 and 49. That is 5 times.

items.prompt: Which numbers from 1 to 40 are in the 5 times table? How many are there?
hints: Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15 ...
What is the last number up to 40?
Count how many numbers you said.
items.explanation: The numbers are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40. That is 8 numbers.

items.prompt: Dina walks from home to school. She can only go right (R) or up (U). She must go 1 step right and 3 steps up. How many different routes can she take?
hints: The route is a list of steps, such as U U U R.
There is only one R. Where can the R go in the list?
The R can be 1st, 2nd, 3rd or 4th.
items.explanation: The one R can be in any of the 4 places in the list, and the other steps are U. So there are 4 routes.

solution.say: The one R can be in any of the 4 places in the list, and the other steps are U.

items.prompt: Dina walks from home to school. She can only go right (R) or up (U). She must go 2 steps right and 2 steps up. How many different routes can she take?
hints: Write each route as a list, such as R R U U.
Put the two R steps in different places in the list of 4.
List them in order: R R U U, R U R U ...
items.explanation: The routes are RRUU, RURU, RUUR, URRU, URUR and UURR. That is 6 routes.

solution.say: The routes are RRUU, RURU, RUUR, URRU, URUR and UURR.

items.prompt: A child climbs 4 steps. She goes up 1 step or 2 steps at a time. How many different ways can she climb the 4 steps?
hints: Count the ways for 1 step, 2 steps and 3 steps first.
1 step: 1 way. 2 steps: 2 ways. 3 steps: 3 ways.
The ways for 4 steps come from the ways for 3 steps and 2 steps.
items.explanation: For 1 step there is 1 way. For 2 steps there are 2 ways. For 3 steps there are 3 ways. For 4 steps the ways are 2 + 3 = 5. They are 1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 1+2+1, 2+1+1 and 2+2.

items.prompt: A fence is 10 m long. A post stands every 2 m, including both ends. How many posts are there?
hints: Find how many gaps of 2 m there are.
Think about how many posts are needed for 5 gaps.
items.explanation: There are 10 / 2 = 5 gaps. A post is needed at both ends of each gap. So there are 5 + 1 = 6 posts.

solution.say: A post is needed at both ends of each gap.

items.prompt: A path is 20 m long. A tree is planted every 5 m, at both ends too. How many trees are there?
hints: Find how many gaps of 5 m there are.
One more tree than gaps, when you plant at both ends.
items.explanation: There are 20 / 5 = 4 gaps. With a tree at both ends, there is 1 more tree than gaps. So there are 5 trees.

solution.say: With a tree at both ends, there is 1 more tree than gaps.

items.prompt: A log is cut into 4 pieces. The cuts take 9 minutes. Each cut takes the same time. How many minutes does it take to make 5 pieces?
hints: How many cuts make 4 pieces?
3 cuts make 4 pieces, and they take 9 minutes.
How long is one cut? How many cuts make 5 pieces?
items.explanation: 4 pieces need 3 cuts. 9 / 3 = 3 minutes for each cut. 5 pieces need 4 cuts, so 4 x 3 = 12 minutes.

solution.say: 5 pieces need 4 cuts, so 4 x 3 = 12 minutes.

items.prompt: A building has stairs between each floor. How many flights do you climb from floor 1 to floor 4?
hints: Count the gaps between floors, not the floors.
From floor 1 to floor 2 is one flight.
Floor 2 to floor 3 is the next.
items.explanation: The flights go 1 to 2, 2 to 3 and 3 to 4. So you climb 3 flights.

solution.say: The flights go 1 to 2, 2 to 3 and 3 to 4.

items.prompt: Ana is 4th from the front of a queue. She is also 5th from the back. How many children are in the queue?
hints: Ana is counted from the front and from the back.
The children in front of Ana are 3.
The children behind Ana are 4.
items.explanation: There are 3 children in front of Ana and 4 children behind her. With Ana, that is 3 + 1 + 4 = 8 children.

solution.say: There are 3 children in front of Ana and 4 children behind her.

items.prompt: Tom is 7th from the front of a queue. He is also 3rd from the back. How many children are in the queue?
hints: Find how many children are in front of Tom.
6 children are in front of Tom. How many are behind him?
Count Tom too.
items.explanation: There are 6 children in front of Tom and 2 behind him. With Tom, that is 6 + 1 + 2 = 9 children.

solution.say: There are 6 children in front of Tom and 2 behind him.

items.prompt: In a line, Ana is 5th and Ben is 12th. How many children stand between Ana and Ben?
hints: Do not count Ana or Ben.
The children between them are 6th, 7th ...
Which is the last place before Ben?
items.explanation: The children are in places 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11. That is 6 children.

solution.say: The children are in places 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11.

items.prompt: A drawer has 4 red socks and 4 blue socks. It is dark. You want 2 socks of the same colour. How many must you take to be sure?
hints: Think about the worst luck you could have.
Your first 2 socks could be different colours.
What colour must the third sock be?
items.explanation: With 2 socks you might have one red and one blue. The third sock must match one of them. So you must take 3 socks.

solution.say: With 2 socks you might have one red and one blue.
The third sock must match one of them.

items.prompt: Count squares of any size on the 4 by 4 board. How many are there?

figure.alt: A square board with 4 rows and 4 columns of small squares.

hints: Count the small squares first. There are 16.
Next count the squares made of 2 by 2 small squares.
There are 9 of those. Then 3 by 3 and 4 by 4.
items.explanation: There are 16 small squares, 9 squares of 2 by 2, 4 squares of 3 by 3 and 1 big square. In all, 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30 squares.

solution.say: There are 16 small squares, 9 squares of 2 by 2, 4 squares of 3 by 3 and 1 big square.
